Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

onestepcox 0.1.0

  • First version, accompanying the article on the one-step closed-form hazard ratio estimator anchored at the Mantel-Haenszel estimator.
  • EstHR() returns the log hazard ratio, the hazard ratio, the standard error, and a Wald confidence interval by eleven methods: the proposed "MH_Halley", the one-step corrections "MH_Newton", "Pike_Halley", "Pike_Newton", "MH_Chebyshev", and "Pike_Chebyshev", the closed-form "MH", "Pike", and "Peto", and the Cox estimate by survival::coxph() ("Cox") or by Newton-Raphson iteration on the same risk-set summaries ("Cox_NR"). Tied event times are handled by the Efron (default) or the Breslow method, and stratification is supported.
  • EstHR() and RiskTable() accept a formula Surv(time, event) ~ group + strata(s) with a data frame, as in survival::coxph(), as well as vectors. EstHR() takes several methods at once and returns an object of class "EstHR" with print() and plot() methods.
  • RiskTable() returns the risk-set summaries shared by the estimators.
  • GenSimData(), carried over from the package accompanying an earlier version of the article, generates stratified data (strata_prop, strata_hazard) and tied times (time_unit). Without these arguments it gives the same data as before for a given seed.
  • CompareOC() reports, for each method, the median, 90th and 99th percentiles, and maximum of the deviation from a reference estimator, the deviation divided by the standard error of the reference, the proportion of replicates whose hazard ratio with two decimals differs from that of the reference, the ratio of the standard errors, the bias, standard deviation, RMSE, mean standard error, and coverage relative to the true hazard ratio, and the computing time. Scenarios may have strata and rounded times.
  • LimitHR() computes the large-sample limits of the estimators under the design of GenSimData().
  • The results of CompareOC() and LimitHR() have classes "CompareOC" and "LimitHR" with print() and plot() methods. The plot() methods of the three classes draw with ‘ggplot2’ and return ggplot objects. They take labels of the methods (by default with hyphens, such as MH-Halley), colors, point shapes and sizes, line types and widths, the base font size, and the position of the legend (outside the panel at the bottom, top, right, or left, or inside it). The legend is below the panel by default for the results of CompareOC() and LimitHR().
  • inst/reproduce/ reproduces Figure 1 of Berry, Kitchin and Mock (1991) and test data 1 of Therneau and Grambsch (2000); inst/validation/ compares the estimators with an independent Python implementation and LimitHR() with large-sample simulations.
  • Vignettes (browseVignettes("onestepcox")): an introduction, the agreement with survival::coxph() and survival::survdiff(), simulations with GenSimData() and CompareOC(), and the large-sample limits of LimitHR().
